title: fix(losses): prevent premature half-precision Hausdorff overflow
body:
## What does this pull request do?

`HausdorffERLoss` and `HausdorffERLoss3D` can produce infinite float16 losses and gradients even when the requested result is representable. The depth weights overflow before multiplication by the soft error or before a spatial mean.

For a 256 x 256 two-class probability map with a 150 x 150 false-positive square at probability 0.875, `k=60, alpha=2` accumulates a depth weight of 73,810. Multiplying by the exact soft error 11/16 gives a representable maximum score of 50,744.375 and an exact mean of 3,143.694793701172. The base returns infinity; the change returns the correctly rounded half mean and finite gradients. A 3-D cube and a tensor exponent have separate closed-form regression oracles. These are synthetic proofs with probabilities in [0, 1]; real-data frequency and training outcomes have not been measured.

Accumulate the weights and weighted errors in float32 for float16/bfloat16 inputs, then restore the original result dtype after the requested reduction. Keep threshold arithmetic and erosion-mask inputs in their original dtype. Preserve scalar/batched tensor-exponent promotion and both `_erode` and `perform_erosion` subclass contracts. Values whose final `none` or `sum` result exceeds the output dtype still overflow normally.

Converting predictions and tensor exponents to float32 before the loss is an existing alternative. This change retains the caller's output dtype and the existing erosion callbacks while computing representable results. A changelog fragment is included.

## Related issue or discussion

The current binary-erosion semantics from #6678 are preserved. This is independent of the older CPU batching and kernel-construction changes. The [complete implementation-history audit](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/blob/91a513ed7a33d94d7fb56c3d4a6a007e360f8ba3/.audit/kornia/hausdorff-complete-history-summary.json) covers upstream PR heads, old fork branches, reachable intermediate commits and historical paths; it found no prior wider-accumulation repair.

## What did you check?

Final head: `c64d52b69702607cd56e914bf1dc931a92ccd8f0`; base: `5cc9c44eddd8dc6a061151d245925f072d673321`.

[Independent CPU validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43972241619) on PyTorch 2.5.1 and 2.15.0, each:

- The 52 new half-precision regression cases give **10 failed, 42 passed** on the exact base. The complete affected eager suite passes **118 cases** with float32/float64 (6 deselected) and **116 cases** with float16/bfloat16 (8 deselected).
- The square/cube references derive depth analytically and use closed-form sums of powers. Mean-gradient checks and a tensor-exponent derivative check use independent formulas; no erosion implementation supplies the expected result.
- **288 contract records** preserve output dtype, shape, errors, gradient metadata and override call behavior. They cover 2-D/3-D, k=0/3, six input dtypes, Python/NumPy/scalar-tensor/batched-tensor exponents, and custom callbacks. Existing unsupported inputs retain their errors. Full-precision and custom-override value records match the base bit for bit; four half-precision numeric records change.
- Full pre-commit and typecheck pass. The final follow-up only adds the measured-cost comment; its production AST is identical to tested head `ec3b52d4`, and the tests are unchanged. Full pre-commit and typecheck were repeated on the final head.

```text
pixi run -e py312 uv run --no-sync pytest tests/losses/test_hd.py --device=cpu --dtype=float32,float64 -k "not jit and not compile and not dynamo and not onnx and not trace and not export" -q
pixi run -e py312 uv run --no-sync pytest tests/losses/test_hd.py --device=cpu --dtype=float16,bfloat16 -k "not jit and not compile and not dynamo and not onnx and not trace and not export" -q
pixi run -e py312 uv run --no-sync pre-commit run --all-files
pixi run -e py312 typecheck
```

Public-API timings use the same Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 runner, one CPU thread, Python 3.12.12, the repository's `warm_up_cpu` and `time_us` helpers, and two base/two candidate rounds in B/C/C/B order. The following are elapsed-time increases for float16, forward / forward+backward:

| Workload, k=10 | Torch 2.5.1 | Torch 2.15.0 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 2 x 2 x 64 x 64 | +8.5% / +9.7% | +6.5% / +7.3% |
| 1 x 2 x 24 x 24 x 24 | +5.4% / +5.9% | +4.7% / +6.8% |

Bfloat16 costs increase 2.4%–6.2% across those workloads/modes; float32 controls range from -1.9% to +0.2%. The precision repair has a measured cost. These CPU samples establish neither accelerator cost nor downstream training benefit. [Machine-readable verification, raw measurements and contract records](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/blob/4892825adee89ae1998ccbe39e4c812d95db7da1/.audit/kornia/hausdorff-final-verification.json).

**Draft validation limit:** the package/importer torch.compile and ONNX conformance selections required by TESTING.md remain unverified. TorchScript, CUDA and MPS are also unverified. The completed eager CPU checks do not replace those gates.

## Which part was done by a human, if any?

Afloat16 set the contribution scope and required new, non-duplicate changes with practical benefit. OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 Astra Pro) performed the technical investigation, implementation and validation reported above; a separate Codex agent reviewed the mathematical, dtype and subclass contracts.

Posted on behalf of @Afloat16 by OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 Astra Pro).
